text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Jean Chretien rules out national tax relief: After deficit is erased, social programs should get any extra money, Chretien says.
- Film law sparks federal cabinet clash: PolyGram Filmed Entertainment seeks exemption.
- Dole hones attack on issue of ethics: Focus turns to political contributions on eve of second presidential debate.
- Ontario Auditor criticizes lax welfare system: Revenue also lost on corporate taxes.
- Newfoundland Premier Brian Tobin reveals secret pact on hydro: Quebec agreed in 1984 to discuss altering deal, Tobin says.
- Market bullish on Canada: International money managers poured more money into the bond market yesterday in response to Canada's recent parade of positive economic news.
- Cadillac Fairview Corp buys T. Eaton Co mall stakes: Developer and partners invest more than C$200 million in four regional shopping centres.
- Wall Street takes a shine to Canada: Fiscal restraint seen as 'way ahead' of U.S.; bond spread hits 11-year low.
- Bre-X faces more claims over gold mine: Partners vie for 40-percent stake.
- Borneo Gold shares plummet: Lose 40 percent of value as trading resumes after month-long halt.

- Vancouver Stock Exchange error lets Cam-Net trade: Mistake at VSE allows shares of the company, whose former CEO is wanted by the FBI, to change hands briefly. They are unlikely to trade again soon.
- General Motors takes fight with CAW to court: GM has filed for court permission to move production equipment from two plants being struck by the CAW.
